title: THE MAN WHO WAS THE ELEVATOR
deck: The lift has stopped with a woman inside and the whole building has chosen its villain. Illuminara cannot carry forty frightened neighbours or force a landlord to buy a motor, so she asks the villain to teach her the one thing he has told nobody.
shape: Six scenes across one hot night: a lobby that has already decided, a door that stays shut, a wheel that corrects her hands and a fear that is finally spoken, a notebook tested against a notebook, a bounded way down that ends with the car tagged out, and a dawn in which the secret becomes a filed, shared claim.

scenes.title: Thirty-Eight Degrees
paragraphs: *Harrow Tower, ground-floor lobby · 00:10, the third night of the heat*

The lift had stopped between the seventh floor and the eighth at 23:52, with Mrs Pell inside it. By ten past midnight the thermometer over the mailboxes said thirty-eight, the machine-room door on the roof had been locked from the inside for twenty minutes, and the lobby of Harrow Tower had sorted its sixty-one households into the ones who were shouting and the ones who were too hot to.
Illuminara had come in off the street for the shade. She stayed because the loudest voice in the room belonged to a woman holding a notebook like a summons.
The fire brigade had been called at 23:58. The dispatcher had put eleven callouts ahead of them in the heat and said an hour, at best.

**Achterberg**  
Dov Lindqvist is sitting behind a locked door while a woman bakes in a steel box. Eighteen months I have been writing to the landlord about this lift, and the whole time Dov has stood where you are standing and told me it was the contractor's timetable.

**Pell**  
Nobody is baking. I am sitting on the floor, which is cooler, and I have my tablets but not my cooler for the insulin. I would like that remembered when you have finished being right at each other.

Her voice came thin through the lobby intercom, from twenty metres up a shaft nobody could see into. Nurse Lowell from the fifth floor was already kneeling at the grille with a wet cloth over one shoulder.

**Lowell**  
Tablets under the tongue now, Mrs Pell, cloth on your neck, and tell me something every five minutes. Sixty-eight, diabetic, forty degrees in a closed car. I can keep her safe for an hour. After that I want her out through any door anyone can open.
Illuminara could take fourteen flights of stairs at a run, and she could carry a person down them without feeling the weight. She said so.

**Achterberg**  
Forty people above the seventh floor, none of them under seventy, and you would carry them down in the dark on a stranger's arm? Half would sooner stay and cook. And if you break that door, it is the hammer that convicts him, not the truth. I want him to open it himself and tell me why my lift crawls.

She pushed the notebook into Illuminara's hands. Six hundred and forty rides, each one timed on a kitchen stopwatch, each with a date, the weather and the minutes. A full run to the top took anywhere between eleven and nineteen.

Illuminara read it under the lobby light, standing very still, and then looked at the caretaker's rota pinned beside the mailboxes. The slow runs were not the landlord's days. They came the morning after Dov's boiler nights, and on the cold wet days that make every old joint in a building complain. *A contractor's timetable is steady. This lift sulks with the weather, the way a man's knees would.*
She said none of it. In that lobby a guess spoken aloud would have been a verdict.

**Illuminara**  
I would like to see the machine room before I tell you what I think.

scenes.title: The Door
paragraphs: *Harrow Tower, roof machine room · 00:35*

She climbed fifteen flights in three minutes and slowed for the last one. At the top she laid her palm flat on the steel door and listened the only way she could, through what the building was made of.

Six ropes hung a car and a counterweight in almost perfect balance. A sheave turned on its shaft under no motor's torque at all. And across it, faint and regular as a pulse, a human weight leaned on a lever. The car's only support was a brake spring, the one thing between Mrs Pell and the pit. *Nothing here is pushing. Something here is holding.*
She sat down in the corridor with her back to the door, in the heat of the building's whole day, and did not knock.

**Illuminara**  
I am not here for the key, Mr Lindqvist, and I will not break your door. When you let off that brake, I can take the car's weight on the ropes for as long as it takes, so nothing can slip while you decide. I will not ask you a question you have not already asked yourself.
For a long time there was only the tick of cooling metal. Then something heavy was set down.

**Dov**  
Who sent you?

**Illuminara**  
Nobody. I would like to learn the wheel.
The bolt slid.

Inside, the heat was forty-four degrees and had weight. A dead motor the size of a bathtub sat under a dust sheet. Bolted to its shaft stub was an iron hand-wheel as wide as a bus wheel, and beside it a brake lever with a length of gas pipe welded on for leverage. On a milk crate between them sat a man of sixty-three with both knees strapped in bandages, soaked through, his hands not quite steady.

**Dov**  
You said the wheel. So you know.

**Illuminara**  
I know the car hangs on the brake and nothing is turning it. I do not know why, and I will not until you tell me.

**Dov**  
The motor burned out four years ago. The landlord's man came with a quote for forty-eight thousand, and the landlord said wait for the budget. There was a woman on nine on oxygen. So I made a wheel.
He looked at the dust sheet, not at her.

**Dov**  
Go and tell them. Sixty-one households, four years, a machine that was a man. They will ask what they have been paying me for. Tell me what I say to that.

**Illuminara**  
I can't give you that sentence. I don't think it exists yet. Show me the wheel first.

scenes.title: Dog on a Lead
paragraphs: *The machine room · 00:50*

He taught it the way it had been taught to him, which was badly and by hand. The counterweight did the lifting. What the car needed was holding: a balanced car wants to run either way, and the whole labour was to stand against it with a brake lever and a wheel for thirteen minutes at a time, then stop it level with the floor to within two fingers. A band of white tape marked each landing on the rope. Eight was the third from the top. Nurse Lowell's rule, shouted down the stairwell and back, was that no door opened until the car sat level on its tape.

**Dov**  
Left hand on the lever, right on the wheel. The lever is the lift. The wheel is only how far.
Illuminara took the lever like a door handle she expected to give, and he reached across and moved her hand.

**Dov**  
Lower. You are holding it like a prize. It is a dog on a lead.

She laughed, which surprised her. The iron was slick with his sweat and hers, the heat pressed on her like a palm, and for the length of that laugh she was only a woman being corrected in a hot room by a man who knew better. *Four years of this. For a hundred and twenty people who thought it was electricity.*

**Illuminara**  
Now. Ease it. I have the weight.

She took the car on the ropes, as she had said she would. The lever came up under her hand and nothing slipped. The wheel turned at a dog's pace, and the third band of tape crept up the rope and settled against its mark. Ninety seconds. A metre.

**Dov**  
Eight.

**Illuminara**  
Eight.
He dropped the lever into its notch. The brake took the car back from her without a sound, and the machine room was only a hot room again.

**Dov**  
The landing key is in my left pocket. Somebody has to open the door, and my knees will not do seven flights.

She took it from his pocket on the way past, and he let her. She was at the eighth-floor door in forty seconds, with Nurse Lowell already beside it, and the car sat level on its tape. Mrs Pell came out into the corridor on her hands and knees like a woman climbing from a swimming pool, and propped herself against the wall with a wet cloth on her neck.

**Pell**  
I always thought that lift had a mind of its own. It turns out it had a man.
Lowell had two fingers on Mrs Pell's wrist already. Illuminara went back up the fifteen flights. Dov had not moved from his crate.

**Dov**  
Now go and tell them. I know what comes next. A man fitted a winch to a passenger lift with a gas pipe and a bus wheel. By lunch the landlord's lawyer has an unlicensed modification and a voided insurance policy, and the car is sealed, and it was me who made it unsafe. I lose the job, and the flat that goes with the job, and then there is nothing at all for the ones who cannot climb.

**Illuminara**  
Mrs Achterberg has six hundred and forty rides timed on a kitchen stopwatch. Your slow days are in her book, and she does not yet know whose they are. A claim built on her book and yours is a claim about this building. It is not one employee's confession. And this key goes to the association tonight, not back to the landlord's man.

**Dov**  
Then nobody seals that car on my word. Nobody's mother gets locked in or out of her flat because of what I did.

**Illuminara**  
That is yours to ask of them. I can't ask it for you.
He looked at the dust sheet for a while. The tick of cooling metal came back.

**Dov**  
Get me a chair. I will tell them myself.

scenes.title: Two Notebooks
paragraphs: *Harrow Tower, lobby · 01:45*

Nobody had told the lobby what had happened on the roof. Dov told it himself. He came down in a chair that two neighbours carried, because his knees would not take the stairs, and set himself in the middle of the floor like a man who has chosen where he will be sentenced.

**Dov**  
The motor burned out four years ago. I have been the lift. Every time anyone on the upper floors got into that car, it was me on the wheel.
Nobody shouted. That was the worst of it, and he knew it.

**Achterberg**  
A man cannot move a lift.

**Dov**  
A man can hold one.

Mrs Achterberg went to the association box and came back with a red binder stamped with the year of the installation, thirty-five years back. She had sat on the committee that bought the lift, and she had kept the commissioning book because nobody else had wanted it.

**Achterberg**  
Rated load six hundred and thirty kilos. The counterweight is the car plus two-fifths of that. Empty, he works against a quarter of a tonne. With four people in it, he works against nothing. He is not lifting a lift. He is holding one back. Slowly. Thirteen minutes to the top.
She shut the binder and opened her notebook instead.

**Achterberg**  
I will not take your word for it, and I will not take hers. I am going to give you three dates from my notebook, Dov. You tell me what your own book says. Without looking at mine.
Dov took a green exercise book from his shirt, damp at the corners, ruled in columns by hand. Mrs Achterberg read out the fourth of March, the twenty-ninth of June, the second of October.

**Dov**  
Fourth of March, cold rain, seventeen minutes, left knee bad. Twenty-ninth of June, dry, eleven and a half, a good day. Second of October, the morning after the boiler, nineteen minutes. I was on a stick.
She looked at her page for some time.

**Achterberg**  
Seventeen-oh-eight. Eleven forty-one. Nineteen-oh-two.
She closed the notebook.

**Achterberg**  
I believe you. That is not the same as forgiving you, and I will not pretend that sixty-one households paid a man to do a job and were told it was a machine.

**Dov**  
I know. And I will not have that car sealed on my word.

**Achterberg**  
It will not be sealed on your word. If it is stopped, it will be stopped on ours, in writing, with both books beside it.

**Illuminara**  
Then the wheel does not stay with one man tonight, and it is not a service. It is a way down for anyone who says yes. Dov holds the brake lever, sitting, because he is the only one who knows how it bites. Pairs turn the wheel, a quarter of an hour each. Four passengers at most. A car a hand's width off its tape only pauses a run: Dov seats the lever, we bring it level again, and nothing opens until it is. Three things end the car for the night and send everyone to the chairs: the lever will not seat, the ropes slip in my hand, or the roof and the landings cannot hear each other. I will have my hand on the ropes for every run. I will not lift. I will be what holds if the brake or your hands do not.

**Lowell**  
I can sign for the people. I cannot sign for the machine. Mrs Achterberg keeps landing keys in that box, and I want one on every landing the car serves, with one of mine standing on it. No door opens on a guess. It opens on two calls from the roof: Dov's, seated, and hers, on the tape. Anyone who would sooner take the stairs gets a chair and two neighbours, and nobody is carried who says no. Nine of mine will not come down at all. They have got fans, a wet sheet and me on the hour.
Illuminara put Dov's landing key into the nurse's hand. Mrs Achterberg, without being asked, unlocked the association box and counted the rest out of a biscuit tin.

**Achterberg**  
Then when the last one is down, that car is out of service until a man with a certificate has signed it. I will write the card.

**Dov**  
I will tie it on.

**Achterberg**  
Let the nine stay. And do not you dare carry them.

**Illuminara**  
I won't.

scenes.title: Quarter of an Hour
paragraphs: *The machine room, then the lobby · 03:00 to 05:20*

By three o'clock there were pairs on the wheel. Dov sat on his milk crate with both legs up on a chair and the lever under his hand, saying lower, and slower, and not like a prize, and for the first time in four years nobody on the roof was alone with the car. Mr Okoro from the ninth took a turn at the wheel and swore at it. Mrs Achterberg took the third turn herself and said afterwards that nobody had told her how the iron fought back.

**Dov**  
Slower, Mr Okoro. It is a dog on a lead.

Illuminara stood at the sheave with one hand on the ropes and did not lift. Twice the car drifted a hand's width off its tape. Twice Dov said stop before she did, and the lever seated, and the two of them walked it back onto its mark before anything went down the stairwell, and she felt the ropes go slack under her palm the way a held breath goes. Neither time did she have to take the weight. She let him call it. Every run the same two calls came down the stairwell, Dov's *seated* and hers, *on the tape*, and the marshals standing on the landing keys turned them only behind both.

Nineteen people came down that night in five runs, and twelve more in chairs on the stairs, each of them having said yes. They sat in the lobby under the fans with their feet in basins. Nine stayed above, with Lowell on the hour.

On the fifth run Dov dropped the lever into its notch for the last time. Mrs Achterberg, who had been waiting for it with a pen, held up a card: OUT OF SERVICE. NOT INSPECTED. BY ORDER OF THE RESIDENTS. Dov, on his stick, tied it to the lever with a bootlace.

Illuminara took her hand off the rope for the first time in two hours, and nothing moved, because nothing needed her to. *An hour ago it was one man's secret.* At the machine-room door she felt it the way you feel a heavy door finally swing on its own hinges.

scenes.title: The Log
paragraphs: *Harrow Tower, lobby, then the housing office · 05:40 to 08:50*

The fire crew came at twenty to six, eleven callouts late and apologetic. They looked at the car sitting level on its tape, read the card on the lever, took Dov's name and the lift's, and said that nobody was to run it again until an engineer had signed it. Nobody needed telling.

At dawn Mrs Achterberg ruled a page in two columns on the mailbox shelf. On the left went Dov's green book, and on the right her own timings, and both were signed in the same pen. Dov went door to door with the page, on a stick, with two neighbours behind him in case his knees gave. Fifty-four households signed. Five did not answer. Two doors did not open. Behind the one on nine somebody turned a radio up, and Dov stood in the corridor a long moment, and then went on to the next.

At twenty to nine Mrs Achterberg, Dov on his stick and Mr Okoro with the commissioning binder under his arm stood at the counter of the housing office. They had copies of both notebooks, the binder's load table, the quote for forty-eight thousand and a page with fifty-four signatures. The clerk read the first sheet twice, stamped the page and printed a receipt: a case number, the date, an emergency inspection booked for Tuesday at nine, the lift to stay out of service until released. It was not a motor. It was a number the landlord's office would have to answer.

The landlord's agent had already left a message on Mrs Achterberg's phone, asking the association to withdraw until the budget was settled. She read it on the tram and did not reply. Dov's knees would not be better by Tuesday, and nobody on the page pretended that two closed doors would open by then.
Illuminara went with them as far as the tram stop and no further. The paper was theirs, and the signatures on it, and the Tuesday that came with it.

Behind her, in Harrow Tower, a neighbour she had never spoken to was carrying a cooler up seven flights to a woman who had not spoken to him in a year, and on the eighth-floor landing the white tape hung level on its rope beside a card tied with a bootlace, and nothing moved.

critic_line: Illuminara first learns what Dov has actually been holding and why he hid it, then makes her power a bounded backstop while Dov, Mrs Achterberg, Lowell and the residents choose and own the rescue, the tag-out and the filing; Mrs Pell is freed, thirty-one consenting residents come down, nine remain under care, and a four-year secret becomes a shared repair claim with a case number and inspection date without erasing Dov's responsibility, the two closed doors or the missing motor.

shared_strengths: Strong concrete premise (a man hand-operating a lift for years), humane problem-solving through dialogue, and a collective resolution that avoids a villain. Some mechanical and procedural exposition mid-story slows pace, but the secret reveal and the notebook cross-check pay off well.

A striking central conceit becomes a humane story about hidden labor, collective responsibility, consent, and evidence. Distinctive dialogue and escalating revelations should sustain this audience, though the lengthy procedural safety planning and repeated operational detail may slow some readers before the emotionally satisfying communal resolution.

translation_sl.title: MOŠKI, KI JE BIL DVIGALO
translation_sl.deck: Dvigalo se je ustavilo z žensko v kabini in vsa stavba je že izbrala svojega krivca. Illuminara ne more odnesti štiridesetih prestrašenih sosedov niti prisiliti lastnika, da kupi motor, zato krivca prosi, naj jo nauči edino stvar, ki je ni povedal nikomur.
translation_sl.shape: Šest prizorov v eni vroči noči: avla, ki se je že odločila, vrata, ki ostajajo zaprta, kolo, ki popravi njene roke, in strah, ki je končno izrečen, zvezek, preverjen z drugim zvezkom, omejena pot navzdol, ki se konča z izločitvijo kabine iz uporabe, ter zora, ko skrivnost postane vložen skupni zahtevek.

scenes.title: Osemintrideset stopinj
paragraphs: *Harrow Tower, avla v pritličju · 00.10, tretja noč vročinskega vala*

Dvigalo se je ob 23.52 ustavilo med sedmim in osmim nadstropjem, v njem pa je bila gospa Pell. Deset minut čez polnoč je termometer nad poštnimi nabiralniki kazal osemintrideset, vrata strojnice na strehi so bila že dvajset minut zaklenjena od znotraj, avla stolpnice Harrow Tower pa je enainšestdeset gospodinjstev razdelila na tista, ki so kričala, in tista, ki jim je bilo prevroče, da bi.
Illuminara je prišla z ulice zaradi sence. Ostala je, ker je najglasnejši glas v prostoru pripadal ženski, ki je držala zvezek kot sodni poziv.
Gasilce so poklicali ob 23.58. Dispečer je prednje v vročini postavil še enajst intervencij in rekel: eno uro, v najboljšem primeru.

**Achterberg**  
Dov Lindqvist sedi za zaklenjenimi vrati, medtem ko se ženska peče v jekleni škatli. Osemnajst mesecev pišem lastniku o tem dvigalu, Dov pa je ves ta čas stal tam, kjer stojite vi, in mi govoril, da je vse odvisno od urnika serviserja.

**Pell**  
Nihče se ne peče. Sedim na tleh, kjer je hladneje, in tablete imam, hladilne torbe za inzulin pa ne. Rada bi, da se tega spomnite, ko boste končali s tem, kdo ima prav.

Njen glas je skozi domofon v avli prihajal slaboten, iz jaška dvajset metrov nad njimi, kamor nihče ni mogel videti. Medicinska sestra Lowell iz petega nadstropja je že klečala ob rešetki z mokro krpo čez ramo.

**Lowell**  
Tableto zdaj pod jezik, gospa Pell, krpo na vrat in vsakih pet minut mi nekaj povejte. Oseminšestdeset let, sladkorna bolezen, štirideset stopinj v zaprti kabini. Eno uro jo lahko varujem. Potem jo hočem ven skozi katerakoli vrata, ki jih kdo lahko odpre.
Illuminara bi lahko v teku premagala štirinajst nadstropij in človeka odnesla navzdol, ne da bi občutila njegovo težo. To je povedala.

**Achterberg**  
Nad sedmim nadstropjem je štirideset ljudi, nihče od njih ni mlajši od sedemdeset let, vi pa bi jih po temi nesli navzdol v naročju tujke? Polovica bi raje ostala in se kuhala. In če razbijete tista vrata, bo njega obsodilo kladivo, ne resnica. Hočem, da jih odpre sam in mi pove, zakaj se moje dvigalo vleče.

Zvezek je potisnila Illuminari v roke. Šeststo štirideset voženj, vsaka izmerjena s kuhinjsko štoparico, pri vsaki datum, vreme in minute. Celotna vožnja do vrha je trajala od enajst do devetnajst minut.

Illuminara ga je prebrala pod lučjo v avli, povsem pri miru, nato pa pogledala razpored hišnika, pripet ob poštnih nabiralnikih. Počasne vožnje niso bile ob dnevih, ko je prihajal lastnik. Pojavile so se zjutraj po Dovovih nočnih izmenah pri kotlu in v hladnih, mokrih dneh, ko se pritoži vsak star sklep v stavbi. *Urnik serviserja je enakomeren. To dvigalo se kuja zaradi vremena, tako kot bi se človekova kolena.*
Ničesar ni rekla. V tisti avli bi ugibanje, izrečeno na glas, postalo razsodba.

**Illuminara**  
Rada bi videla strojnico, preden vam povem, kaj mislim.

scenes.title: Vrata
paragraphs: *Harrow Tower, strojnica na strehi · 00.35*

V treh minutah se je povzpela petnajst nadstropij in pred zadnjim upočasnila. Na vrhu je položila dlan na jeklena vrata in prisluhnila tako, kot je lahko le ona, skozi snov, iz katere je bila zgrajena stavba.

Šest vrvi je držalo kabino in protiutež v skoraj popolnem ravnovesju. Vrvnica se je vrtela na gredi brez kakršnegakoli navora motorja. In čeznjo je rahlo in enakomerno kot utrip človeška teža pritiskala na vzvod. Kabino je držala le vzmet zavore, edina stvar med gospo Pell in dnom jaška. *Nič tukaj ne potiska. Nekaj tukaj zadržuje.*
Sedla je na hodnik s hrbtom ob vratih, v vročini vsega stavbinega dneva, in ni potrkala.

**Illuminara**  
Nisem prišla po ključ, gospod Lindqvist, in vaših vrat ne bom razbila. Ko boste popustili zavoro, lahko prevzamem težo kabine na vrveh za toliko časa, kolikor ga potrebujete za odločitev, tako da nič ne more zdrsniti. Ne bom vam zastavila vprašanja, ki si ga niste že sami.
Dolgo se je slišalo le tiktakanje kovine, ki se je hladila. Potem je nekdo odložil nekaj težkega.

**Dov**  
Kdo vas je poslal?

**Illuminara**  
Nihče. Rada bi se naučila uporabljati kolo.
Zapah se je odmaknil.

V notranjosti je bilo štiriinštirideset stopinj in vročina je imela težo. Mrtvi motor, velik kot kopalna kad, je stal pod ponjavo. Na štrclju njegove gredi je bilo pritrjeno železno ročno kolo, široko kot avtobusno kolo, ob njem pa zavorni vzvod, na katerega je bila za daljšo ročico privarjena plinska cev. Na zaboju za mleko med njima je sedel triinšestdesetletni moški z obema kolenoma v povojih, premočen, z rokami, ki niso bile povsem mirne.

**Dov**  
Rekli ste kolo. Torej veste.

**Illuminara**  
Vem, da kabina visi na zavori in da je nič ne poganja. Zakaj, pa ne vem in ne bom vedela, dokler mi ne poveste.

**Dov**  
Motor je pregorel pred štirimi leti. Lastnikov človek je prišel s predračunom za oseminštirideset tisoč, lastnik pa je rekel, naj počakamo na proračun. V devetem nadstropju je živela ženska na kisiku. Zato sem naredil kolo.
Pogledal je ponjavo, ne nje.

**Dov**  
Pojdite in jim povejte. Enainšestdeset gospodinjstev, štiri leta, stroj, ki je bil človek. Vprašali bodo, za kaj so me plačevali. Povejte mi, kaj naj jim odgovorim.

**Illuminara**  
Tega stavka vam ne morem dati. Mislim, da še ne obstaja. Najprej mi pokažite kolo.

scenes.title: Pes na povodcu
paragraphs: *Strojnica · 00.50*

Naučil jo je tako, kot so nekoč naučili njega, torej slabo in z rokami. Dvigala je protiutež. Kabino je bilo treba zadrževati: uravnotežena kabina hoče steči v katerokoli smer, celotno delo pa je bilo upirati se ji z zavornim vzvodom in kolesom po trinajst minut naenkrat ter jo nato ustaviti poravnano s tlemi na dva prsta natančno. Trak belega lepilnega traku je na vrvi označeval vsako nadstropje. Osmo je bilo tretje od vrha. Pravilo medicinske sestre Lowell, ki se je po stopnišču prenašalo s kričanjem gor in dol, je bilo, da se nobena vrata ne odprejo, dokler kabina ni poravnana s trakom.

**Dov**  
Leva roka na vzvodu, desna na kolesu. Vzvod je dvigalo. Kolo določa samo, kako daleč.
Illuminara je prijela vzvod kot kljuko, za katero je pričakovala, da bo popustila, on pa je segel čez in ji premaknil roko.

**Dov**  
Nižje. Držite ga kot trofejo. To je pes na povodcu.

Zasmejala se je, kar jo je presenetilo. Železo je bilo spolzko od njegovega in njenega znoja, vročina je pritiskala nanjo kot dlan, in za dolžino tistega smeha je bila le ženska, ki jo je v vroči sobi popravljal moški, ki je vedel bolje. *Štiri leta tega. Za sto dvajset ljudi, ki so mislili, da jih prevaža elektrika.*

**Illuminara**  
Zdaj. Počasi popustite. Jaz držim težo.

Kabino je prevzela na vrveh, kot je obljubila. Vzvod se je dvignil pod njeno roko in nič ni zdrsnilo. Kolo se je vrtelo s hitrostjo psa, tretji trak pa je polzel po vrvi navzgor in se ustavil ob oznaki. Devetdeset sekund. En meter.

**Dov**  
Osem.

**Illuminara**  
Osem.
Vzvod je spustil v zarezo. Zavora je kabino brez glasu prevzela nazaj od nje in strojnica je bila spet le vroča soba.

**Dov**  
Ključ za vrata na postaji je v mojem levem žepu. Nekdo mora odpreti vrata, moja kolena pa ne zmorejo sedmih nadstropij.

Na poti mimo ga je vzela iz njegovega žepa in on ji je pustil. Pri vratih osmega nadstropja je bila v štiridesetih sekundah, medicinska sestra Lowell pa je že stala ob njih; kabina je mirovala poravnana s trakom. Gospa Pell je po vseh štirih prišla iz kabine na hodnik kot ženska, ki pleza iz bazena, in se naslonila na steno z mokro krpo na vratu.

**Pell**  
Vedno sem mislila, da ima to dvigalo svojo glavo. Izkazalo se je, da je imelo človeka.
Lowell ji je že tipala utrip z dvema prstoma. Illuminara se je vrnila po petnajstih nadstropjih. Dov se ni premaknil z zaboja.

**Dov**  
Zdaj pa pojdite in jim povejte. Vem, kaj sledi. Človek je v potniško dvigalo vgradil vitel s plinsko cevjo in avtobusnim kolesom. Do kosila bo imel lastnikov odvetnik nedovoljeno predelavo in neveljavno zavarovanje, kabina bo zapečatena, nevarno pa sem jo naredil jaz. Izgubim službo in stanovanje, ki gre z njo, potem pa ne ostane nič za tiste, ki ne morejo po stopnicah.

**Illuminara**  
Gospa Achterberg ima šeststo štirideset voženj, izmerjenih s kuhinjsko štoparico. Vaši počasni dnevi so v njenem zvezku in še ne ve, čigavi so. Zahtevek, zgrajen na njenem in vašem zvezku, je zahtevek o tej stavbi. Ni izpoved enega zaposlenega. In ta ključ gre nocoj združenju, ne nazaj lastnikovemu človeku.

**Dov**  
Potem nihče ne zapečati te kabine samo na mojo besedo. Nobena mati ne ostane ujeta v svojem stanovanju ali zunaj njega zaradi tega, kar sem storil.

**Illuminara**  
To morate zahtevati vi. Tega ne morem zahtevati namesto vas.
Nekaj časa je gledal ponjavo. Tiktakanje ohlajajoče se kovine se je vrnilo.

**Dov**  
Prinesite mi stol. Sam jim bom povedal.

scenes.title: Dva zvezka
paragraphs: *Harrow Tower, avla · 01.45*

Nihče avli ni povedal, kaj se je zgodilo na strehi. Dov ji je povedal sam. Navzdol je prišel na stolu, ki sta ga nosila dva soseda, ker njegova kolena niso zmogla stopnic, in se postavil na sredo prostora kot človek, ki je sam izbral kraj svoje obsodbe.

**Dov**  
Motor je pregorel pred štirimi leti. Jaz sem bil dvigalo. Vsakič, ko je kdo iz zgornjih nadstropij vstopil v tisto kabino, sem bil jaz za kolesom.
Nihče ni kričal. To je bilo najhuje in on je to vedel.

**Achterberg**  
Človek ne more premikati dvigala.

**Dov**  
Človek ga lahko zadržuje.

Gospa Achterberg je odšla do omare združenja in se vrnila z rdečim registratorjem, na katerem je bilo leto namestitve, petintrideset let nazaj. Sedela je v odboru, ki je kupil dvigalo, in hranila zapisnik ob zagonu, ker ga nihče drug ni hotel.

**Achterberg**  
Nazivna nosilnost je šeststo trideset kilogramov. Protiutež je masa kabine plus dve petini tega. Ko je prazna, se upira četrt tone. S štirimi ljudmi v njej se ne upira ničemur. Dvigala ne dviguje. Zadržuje ga. Počasi. Trinajst minut do vrha.
Registrator je zaprla in namesto njega odprla svoj zvezek.

**Achterberg**  
Ne bom verjela vam in ne bom verjela njej. Iz svojega zvezka vam bom dala tri datume, Dov. Vi mi povejte, kaj piše v vašem. Ne da bi pogledali mojega.
Dov je iz srajce potegnil zelen šolski zvezek, vlažen na robovih in ročno razdeljen v stolpce. Gospa Achterberg je prebrala četrti marec, devetindvajseti junij in drugi oktober.

**Dov**  
Četrtega marca, mrzel dež, sedemnajst minut, slabo levo koleno. Devetindvajsetega junija, suho, enajst in pol, dober dan. Drugega oktobra, jutro po kotlu, devetnajst minut. Imel sem palico.
Dolgo je gledala svojo stran.

**Achterberg**  
Sedemnajst nič osem. Enajst enainštirideset. Devetnajst nič dve.
Zaprla je zvezek.

**Achterberg**  
Verjamem vam. To ni isto kot odpuščanje in ne bom se pretvarjala, da je enainšestdeset gospodinjstev plačevalo človeka za delo, povedali pa so jim, da ga opravlja stroj.

**Dov**  
Vem. In ne bom dovolil, da to kabino zapečatijo samo na mojo besedo.

**Achterberg**  
Ne bo zapečatena na vašo besedo. Če jo bomo ustavili, jo bomo ustavili na našo, pisno, z obema zvezkoma ob njej.

**Illuminara**  
Potem kolo nocoj ne ostane pri enem človeku in to ni storitev. To je pot navzdol za vsakogar, ki reče da. Dov sede drži zavorni vzvod, ker edini ve, kako prime. Pari vrtijo kolo, vsak po četrt ure. Največ štirje potniki. Če je kabina za širino dlani odmaknjena od svojega traku, to samo prekine vožnjo: Dov namesti vzvod, spet jo poravnamo in nič se ne odpre, dokler ni poravnana. Tri stvari končajo uporabo kabine za to noč in vse preusmerijo na stole: vzvod se ne namesti, vrvi mi zdrsnejo v roki ali pa se streha in nadstropja ne slišijo. Pri vsaki vožnji bom imela roko na vrveh. Ne bom dvigovala. Držala bom, če zavora ali vaše roke ne bodo.

**Lowell**  
Lahko podpišem za ljudi. Ne morem podpisati za stroj. Gospa Achterberg hrani ključe za vrata nadstropij v tisti omari in na vsakem nadstropju, kjer se ustavi kabina, hočem enega svojega človeka s ključem. Nobena vrata se ne odprejo na ugibanje. Odprejo se po dveh klicih s strehe: Dovovem, nameščeno, in njenem, na traku. Vsakdo, ki bi raje šel po stopnicah, dobi stol in dva soseda, nihče pa ne bo prenesen brez svojega da. Devet mojih ne bo šlo dol. Imajo ventilatorje, mokro rjuho in mene vsako uro.
Illuminara je Dovov ključ položila medicinski sestri v roko. Gospa Achterberg je brez prošnje odklenila omaro združenja in iz pločevinaste škatle za piškote preštela preostale.

**Achterberg**  
Ko bo zadnji spodaj, bo ta kabina izločena iz uporabe, dokler je ne podpiše človek s certifikatom. Jaz bom napisala karton.

**Dov**  
Jaz ga bom privezal.

**Achterberg**  
Naj jih devet ostane. In niti pomislite ne, da bi jih nesli.

**Illuminara**  
Ne bom.

scenes.title: Četrt ure
paragraphs: *Strojnica, nato avla · od 03.00 do 05.20*

Ob treh so ob kolesu stali pari. Dov je sedel na zaboju za mleko z obema nogama na stolu in vzvodom pod roko ter govoril nižje, počasneje in ne kot trofejo; prvič po štirih letih na strehi nihče ni bil sam s kabino. Gospod Okoro iz devetega nadstropja je zavrtel kolo in ga preklel. Gospa Achterberg je sama prevzela tretjo izmeno in pozneje rekla, da ji nihče ni povedal, kako se železo upira.

**Dov**  
Počasneje, gospod Okoro. To je pes na povodcu.

Illuminara je stala ob vrvnici z eno roko na vrveh in ni dvigovala. Dvakrat je kabina za širino dlani zdrsnila mimo svojega traku. Dvakrat je Dov ukazal stop, še preden je to storila ona, vzvod se je namestil, skupaj sta kabino vrnila na oznako, preden je karkoli šlo po stopnišču navzdol, ona pa je pod dlanjo začutila, kako so se vrvi sprostile kot zadržani dih. Nobenkrat ji ni bilo treba prevzeti teže. Pustila je, da je ukazal on. Pri vsaki vožnji sta se po stopnišču spustila ista klica, Dovov *nameščeno* in njen *na traku*, redarji ob ključih nadstropij pa so jih obrnili šele po obeh.

Tisto noč se je v petih vožnjah spustilo devetnajst ljudi, še dvanajst pa na stolih po stopnicah, vsak od njih po svojem da. Sedeli so v avli pod ventilatorji z nogami v lavorjih. Devet jih je ostalo zgoraj, Lowell pa jih je obiskovala vsako uro.

Med peto vožnjo je Dov še zadnjič spustil vzvod v zarezo. Gospa Achterberg, ki je čakala s pisalom, je dvignila karton: IZLOČENO IZ UPORABE. NI PREGLEDANO. PO ODLOČBI STANOVALCEV. Dov ga je oprt na palico z vezalko privezal na vzvod.

Illuminara je prvič po dveh urah odmaknila roko z vrvi in nič se ni premaknilo, ker je nihče več ni potreboval. *Pred eno uro je bila to skrivnost enega človeka.* Pri vratih strojnice je to občutila tako, kot čutiš, ko se težka vrata končno sama zazibljejo na tečajih.

scenes.title: Dnevnik
paragraphs: *Harrow Tower, avla, nato stanovanjski urad · od 05.40 do 08.50*

Gasilci so prišli dvajset minut do šestih, enajst intervencij prepozno, in se opravičevali. Pogledali so kabino, ki je mirovala poravnana s trakom, prebrali karton na vzvodu, zapisali Dovovo ime in oznako dvigala ter rekli, da ga nihče ne sme več zagnati, dokler ga ne podpiše inženir. Tega ni bilo treba nikomur povedati dvakrat.

Ob zori je gospa Achterberg na polici za poštne nabiralnike razdelila stran v dva stolpca. Na levo je šel Dovov zeleni zvezek, na desno njene meritve časov, oba pa sta bila podpisana z istim pisalom. Dov je s palico hodil od vrat do vrat s stranjo v roki, dva soseda pa sta mu sledila, če bi mu odpovedala kolena. Štiriinpetdeset gospodinjstev je podpisalo. Pet jih ni odgovorilo. Dvoje vrat se ni odprlo. Za enimi v devetem nadstropju je nekdo glasneje vključil radio, Dov pa je dolgo stal na hodniku in nato odšel do naslednjih.

Dvajset minut do devetih so gospa Achterberg, Dov s palico in gospod Okoro z registratorjem o zagonu pod roko stali pri okencu stanovanjskega urada. Imeli so kopije obeh zvezkov, tabelo obremenitev iz registratorja, predračun za oseminštirideset tisoč in stran s štiriinpetdesetimi podpisi. Uradnik je prvi list prebral dvakrat, ga ožigosal in natisnil potrdilo: številko zadeve, datum, nujni pregled v torek ob devetih, dvigalo pa mora ostati izločeno iz uporabe do dovoljenja. To ni bil motor. Bila je številka, na katero bo moral odgovoriti lastnikov urad.

Lastnikov zastopnik je gospe Achterberg že pustil sporočilo in združenje prosil, naj zahtevek umakne, dokler se ne uredi proračun. Prebrala ga je na tramvaju in ni odgovorila. Dovova kolena do torka ne bodo boljša in nihče na tisti strani se ni pretvarjal, da se bodo do takrat odprla dvoje zaprta vrata.
Illuminara je šla z njimi do tramvajske postaje in nič dlje. Papir je bil njihov, podpisi na njem njihovi in prav tako torek, ki je prišel z njim.

Za njo je v Harrow Tower sosed, s katerim že leto dni nista spregovorila, po sedmih nadstropjih nosil hladilno torbo ženski, v osmem nadstropju pa je ob kartonu, privezanem z vezalko, beli trak visel poravnan na vrvi in nič se ni premikalo.

translation_sl.critic_line: Illuminara najprej razume, kaj je Dov v resnici zadrževal in zakaj je to skrival, nato pa svojo moč uporabi kot omejeno varovalo, medtem ko Dov, gospa Achterberg, Lowell in stanovalci sami izberejo ter prevzamejo reševanje, izločitev dvigala iz uporabe in vložitev prijave; gospa Pell je rešena, enaintrideset stanovalcev se s soglasjem spusti, devet jih ostane pod oskrbo, štiriletna skrivnost pa postane skupni zahtevek za popravilo s številko zadeve in datumom pregleda, ne da bi izbrisali Dovovo odgovornost, dvoje zaprtih vrat ali manjkajoči motor.
